verdicts.reason: A sets the headline on one line at a strong size that fills the banner width, with the tagline centred below and even side margins. Only the vertical spacing could use slight tightening. B is correct but timid: the headline is noticeably smaller and leaves wide dead bands on the left and right, so it reads like a shrunk copy instead of a layout built for the banner.

A pushes the whole text block into the left half and leaves the right half of the canvas empty. The headline wraps so 'sunset.' sits alone on its own line, and that line is centred on a different axis from the first. B is centred and sits on one line with the right hierarchy, but the headline is undersized for the canvas and leaves a lot of empty space at the sides.

A is centred and larger, but it wraps the headline in a wide banner and leaves 'sunset.' orphaned on line two. That breaks up the 'Sip at sunset' phrase and wastes the horizontal format. B keeps the headline intact on one line with a clean tagline beneath it, though its type is small and the side margins are large and empty.
